items.abstract: Wang, Lawrence K. 王抗曝 (2026). Dragon² (龖): From Mahjong's "Double Dragon Embrace" to Peaceful U.S.–China Coexistence and Peace Under Heaven-- A Life-Writing Narrative 《龖(Dragon²): 從麻將「雙龍抱」到中美和平共存與天下太平的生命書寫》. Evolutionary Progress in Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts and Mathematics. Lenox Institute Press, Massachusetts, USA. 8(10L), 43 pages. ........ ABSTRACT: 本文延續作者對「囍—𩺰—龖」的文化思考,將古字「龖」重新詮釋為 Dragon²(亦寫作 Dragon2)。囍象徵新婚之喜,𩺰象徵夫妻無論順境逆境皆相伴一生;龖則將關懷由家庭延伸至世界。在本文所採用的麻將規則中,「雙龍抱」指由兩對相同順子構成的組合,共含四副順子,每對中的兩副順子花色與數序相同。作者借其「抱而不鬥」的意象,將兩龍比喻為具有全球影響力的中國與美國,寄託兩國相互尊重、和平共存的願望。這是作者提出的跨文化和平隱喻,並非將龍視為美國固有的國家象徵。作者於龍年出生於中國,1949年遷至臺灣,後赴美求學、成家與工作。中國承載其出生、文化與早年記憶,臺灣見證其成長與求學,美國則承載其深造、事業與家庭生活。這段跨越海峽與太平洋的生命歷程,使中美關係成為與自身及家人命運相連的切身議題。本文比較「雙龍爭珠」「雙龍戲珠」「雙龍抱」與「雙龍護珠」的意象:若明珠代表霸權,兩龍可能陷入零和競爭;若明珠代表地球,兩龍便肩負共同守護的責任。文章進一步借用工程系統中的回饋、穩定與失控概念,闡述核戰無真正贏家的警示,主張中美競而不戰、強而有制、和而不同,並在氣候變遷、公共衛生、人工智慧安全與核風險降低等領域推動合作。和平的意義亦須落實於平民百姓的生活,使家庭免於戰亂、人民安居樂業、世代得以延續。「龖」為既有古漢字,由兩個繁體「龍」左右並列而成。本文賦予其「雙龍抱,雙吉祥,共築人間仙境」的文化新意,以兩龍相擁、彼此尊重,象徵雙重吉祥、和諧共存與天下太平。此一意涵及其中的中美合作寓意,均屬作者的現代文化詮釋,而非「龖」字的傳統字典釋義; 關鍵詞:龖;Dragon²;Dragon2;雙龍抱;麻將文化;囍;𩺰;中美關係;生命書寫;系統工程;核風險降低;世界和平;和諧共存;天下太平;雙重吉祥;平民福祉;中美合作; ABSTRACT: This article continues the author's cultural reflections on the sequence 囍–𩺰–龖, reinterpreting the ancient Chinese character 龖 as Dragon² (also written as Dragon2). 囍 symbolizes the joy of marriage, while 𩺰 represents lifelong companionship through prosperity and adversity. 龖 extends this concern from the family to the world. In the mahjong rules adopted here, "Double Dragon Embrace" consists of two pairs of identical sequences—four sequences in total, with the two sequences in each pair matching in both suit and numerical order. Drawing on the image of "embracing rather than fighting," the author uses the two dragons as a metaphor for China and the United States, two globally influential powers, expressing the hope that they will respect each other and coexist peacefully. This is a cross-cultural metaphor for peace proposed by the author, not a claim that the dragon is a traditional national symbol of the United States. Born in China in the Year of the Dragon, the author moved to Taiwan in 1949 and later pursued further education, established a family, and developed his career in the United States. China holds his birthplace, cultural roots, and early memories; Taiwan shaped his upbringing and education; and the United States became the setting for his advanced studies, career, and family life. This life journey across the Taiwan Strait and the Pacific makes U.S.–China relations a deeply personal concern connected to his own and his family's future. The article compares four images: "Two Dragons Contending for a Pearl," "Two Dragons Playing with a Pearl," "Double Dragon Embrace," and "Two Dragons Protecting a Pearl." If the pearl represents hegemony, the dragons may become trapped in zero-sum competition; if it represents the Earth, they share a responsibility to protect it. Drawing further on the engineering concepts of feedback, stability, and loss of control, the article emphasizes that nuclear war has no true winners. It advocates competition without warfare, strength exercised with restraint, and harmony without uniformity, alongside cooperation on climate change, public health, artificial intelligence safety, and nuclear risk reduction. Peace must also take concrete form in the lives of ordinary people, allowing families to live free from war, communities to thrive, and future generations to flourish. The character 龖 consists of two traditional Chinese 龍 characters placed side by side. The author gives it a new cultural meaning: "Two dragons embrace, bringing paired blessings and together creating an earthly paradise." Their embrace and mutual respect symbolize shared auspiciousness, harmonious coexistence, and peace under heaven. These meanings, including the association with U.S.–China cooperation, are the author's contemporary cultural interpretation rather than traditional dictionary definitions of 龖. items.title: Human-in-the-Loop Intelligent Automation: A Review of Trust, Oversight, and Workforce Implications
items.abstract: Intelligent automation is now used to retrieve information, predict, recommend, generate content, route workflows and take physical or administrative action. Human-in-the-loop (HITL) design is often suggested as a possible fail-safe but it does not necessarily mean that a person is always in control. Oversight can be undermined by lack of time, authority, competence, independent evidence, or feedback or by a lack of real accountability despite the title of oversight. In this paper we explore HITL intelligent automation from three intertwined perspectives: calibrated trust, operational oversight, and workforce implications. It combines existing human-automation research, guidance for human–AI interaction, risk-management standards, regulation, and evidence of labor. A threat model encompasses technical misfortune, adversarial manipulation, cognitive and organizational failure, and harmful deployment of workforce. The mathematical formulation determines the automation modes based on expected error consequence, uncertainty, review cost, workload and skill preservation. The suggested architecture is that of separating the execution of the model from the risk routing, human decision making, dual authorization, audit, appeal, and learning feedback. A seeded synthetic experiment with 10,000 binary decisions is conducted for the comparisons between automation-only, passive universal review, risk-adaptive HITL, and dual control. With the declared generator, adaptive review achieves a 83.6% to 85.0% accuracy rate, while reviewing 37.1% of cases, and dual control achieves a 87.0% accuracy rate with a 5.2% rate of high impact error. These are indicative values and not measurements taken in the workplace. The review finds that effective HITL systems must have meaningful intervention capability, calibrated reliance, representative evaluation, protected worker voice, continuous competence and evidence of oversight functioning under realistic workload and failure.

items.title: Stability of Tenure: Is Contractualization a Cure?
items.abstract: The library profession has evolved from being traditional bookkeepers to being modern end users of digital data and Artificial Intelligence (AI), over the years. But throughout development, libraries are facing a major crisis: a severe shortage of permanent staff. Administrative bodies are hiring outsourced and temporary staff for most of their work to maintain daily functions as much as possible. This paper critically evaluates the trend of contract hiring, under the title “Stability of Tenure: is contractualization a cure? “However, contract hiring may be a fast & temporary remedy to the problem of vacant positions, but it is disaster to the core essence of the library profession. The libraries need highly skilled, permanent experts to manage complex tasks, relying on temporary staff risks the dignity of profession and user trust. The paper concludes by urging policymakers to invest in stable, permanent jobs to protect the future of libraries.

items.title: The Agent Internet A New Evolutionary Phase of the Web and Its Global Impact
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) based software agents are transitioning from one shot assistants to long term actors that plan, negotiate and accomplish tasks with multiple services. This transformation is resulting in what researchers call the Agent Internet, the Agentic Web or the Internet of Agents, in which programs are full-fledged players alongside people. This article summarizes academic surveys, industry studies and public market data from 2025 to 2026 to outline the multi-layered nature of this setup and to consider its pros and cons. According to market estimates, the revenue for agent software is estimated to be around eight billion dollars in 2025 and up to 35-53 billion dollars in 2030. Adoption statistics tell a tale of much experimentation and few pilots taking it to scale. We discuss communication protocols that enable agents to find and trust each other, the as yet undeveloped identity and payment layers and the burden of agent traffic on advertising supported content. But the challenges that we see are not just capabilities, but security, accountability, interoperability, and who pays for content and compute. Finally, we highlight some of the current research and policy gaps and suggest avenues for a responsible construction.

従来の選挙競争に関する統計力学的モデルは、一般に二値イジングスピン仕様($s_{i}\in\{+1,-1\}$)に依拠しているが、これは一定の投票参加恒等式($s_{i}^{2}\equiv1$)を課すものであり、外生的な政策ショックや評判ショックが直接的なイデオロギーの転向のみを通じて選挙結果を変化させることを前提としている。この制約を緩和し、有権者の戦略的棄権($s_{i}=0$)を内生化するため、本研究では米国50州の空間ネットワーク上に、多項ロジット型量子応答均衡(QRE)と結合した3状態スピン1 items.title: AI-Driven Dynamic Trust in Zero Trust Architecture: A Systematic Literature Review of Machine Learning, Federated Learning and Governance Challenges
items.abstract: Sophisticated cyber threats have exposed the limits of perimeter-based security models, and Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA) has increasingly been adopted as an alternative paradigm. Purpose: This Systematic Literature Review examines the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) within Zero Trust frameworks, covering dynamic trust scoring, behavioural analytics and federated learning, the latter treated as one strand of AI rather than a separate paradigm. Following PRISMA 2020, 22 studies published between 2022 and 2025 were identified across IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, SpringerLink, MDPI and Nature/Scientific Reports, appraised against a five-criterion quality instrument and synthesised narratively. The studies included are few and heterogeneous, and their findings should be read accordingly. Ensemble and hybrid designs predominate (14 of 22). Twelve studies report quantitative results, of which only eight evaluate on real named datasets; reported accuracies of 95 to 99 per cent come from different datasets, tasks, threat models, and evaluation settings, and are neither directly comparable nor a field-level benchmark. Only three studies directly compare learned adaptive trust against a static rule-based baseline. No study reports live operational deployment. We identify thirteen technique categories, eleven implementation barriers, and seven emerging trends. This paper proposes an integrated eight-component framework for AI-driven dynamic trust management, along with a five-domain research agenda. The framework is conceptual and synthesis-derived and requires empirical validation before operational use.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Next-Generation Firewalls for Discriminating Cyber Attacks from Legitimate Service Traffic Surges
items.abstract: Next-generation firewalls (NGFWs) sit on the critical path between public networks and production services. Their most consequential error is no longer a missed signature; it is the inability to tell a malicious flood from a genuine surge in legitimate demand. Flash crowds, seasonal campaigns, media-driven spikes, and elastic microservice fan-out can resemble distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) traffic in volume while remaining economically and operationally valid. Static access-control lists, fixed rate limits, and signature catalogs therefore produce an unacceptable trade-off: either they under-block stealthy application-layer attacks or they over-block paying users. This article reviews, compares, and synthesizes peer-reviewed evidence from 2020 onward on machine-learning and deep-learning methods that can be embedded in NGFW and software-defined enforcement points to discriminate attacks from legitimate service-intensity bursts. We organize the literature into statistical filters, classical classifiers, representation-learning hybrids, sequential models, and two-tier designs that first cheaply detect a burst and then classify its intent. Published detectors regularly report accuracy above 98% on CICDDoS2019 and related traces, yet most benchmarks omit a dedicated flash-event class, which inflates apparent performance and leaves the operationally hardest decision under-tested. Building on that gap, we propose AID-NGFW, a three-tier architecture that couples entropy and cumulative-sum screening with a calibrated three-class discriminator (benign, flash crowd, attack) and a policy engine that drops malicious flows while scaling or shaping legitimate surges. Comparative tables and figures compile reported accuracies, F1-scores, datasets, and latency–accuracy trade-offs. We argue that the scientific and engineering priority is no longer binary attack detection in isolation, but reliable, low-latency, and explainable discrimination under encrypted traffic, class imbalance, concept drift, and adversarial mimicry.

items.title: Bayesian hierarchical downscaling of station observations with learned covariance kernels: an artificial intelligence evaluation of uncertainty propagation in national climate normals
items.abstract: National climate normals are typically reported as single numbers, yet they inherit uncertainty from sparse station networks, interpolation choices and covariance assumptions. The framework is applied to NASA POWER monthly reanalysis air temperature at 2 m for Lagos, Nigeria (6.52°N, 3.38°E) over 2000–2023, comprising 312 monthly observations with a mean of 26.414 °C and a standard deviation of 0.943 °C. The warming trend is estimated at 0.1553 °C per decade. A hierarchical model with a Matérn covariance whose smoothness and length-scale are inferred from the data is compared against fixed-kernel alternatives, and the resulting posterior predictive variance is decomposed into components attributable to the kernel, the trend and the residual. Kernel learning changes the width of the 95% credible band for annual means by a non-trivial margin and that fixed-kernel downscaling systematically under-reports uncertainty at the decadal scale. The contribution is a formal propagation model that makes the kernel a first-class inferential object, together with a diagnostic that flags when national normals are reported with false precision.

items.title: Conformalized graph neural network emulation of regional climate extremes: an artificial intelligence evaluation of coverage guarantees under emissions-scenario shift
items.abstract: Conformal prediction offers distribution-free coverage guarantees for machine-learning emulators of climate extremes, but the guarantee is only as good as the exchangeability assumption that underwrites it. Using NASA POWER monthly reanalysis for Kampala, Uganda (0.35°N, 32.58°E) over 2000–2023 (312 observations, mean 22.443 °C, linear trend −0.1564 °C per decade), the study specifies a graph construction, a split-conformal calibration protocol, and a coverage-degradation bound expressed as a function of a scenario-shift divergence. The analysis derives a finite-sample coverage gap under covariate shift, proposes a weighted conformal score that restores approximate validity, and identifies the conditions under which GNN emulators of regional extremes can be certified for out-of-distribution emissions scenarios. The contribution is a formal account of when conformal coverage survives scenario shift and a diagnostic that practitioners can compute before deploying an emulator.

items.title: Counterfactual crop-yield attribution to seasonal forecast advisories via doubly robust estimation: an artificial intelligence evaluation of adoption-selection bias in extension targeting
items.abstract: Seasonal forecast advisories are promoted as a climate service that raises crop yields, yet extension agencies typically target farmers who already differ from non-adopters in ways that also affect yield. the present analysis formalises the resulting adoption-selection bias and evaluates a doubly robust estimator for counterfactual yield attribution under a declared data-generating process. The design is a replication-based evaluation: 600 data sets of N = 500 were drawn from a process with intercept 12.0, exposure 0.42, group -3.1, severity 1.35 and error SD 4.2, and the ordinary least squares estimator was characterised across replications. The estimated bias was -0.04629 for the intercept and 0.00086 for the exposure coefficient; the root mean squared errors were 0.95661 and 0.01664 respectively, and empirical coverage of the nominal 95% confidence intervals was 1.0 for both parameters. The results indicate that under correct specification the estimator recovers the exposure effect with negligible bias and conservative coverage, but that the intercept is the fragile quantity when group composition is unbalanced. Doubly robust attribution is defensible for advisory evaluation only when the selection model is reported alongside the outcome model, and it derives the conditions under which extension targeting can be interpreted as a counterfactual yield effect rather than a description of adopters.

items.title: Mapping Artificial Intelligence for Personalised Learning based on Learning Style: Scopus-Based Bibliometric Analysis (2006-2026)
items.abstract: The aims of this study is to conduct a bibliometric analysis of the development of learning style-based personalisation. The rapid advancement of AI-based learning personalisation has been accompanied by growing research attention to the role of learning style in the modern learning ecosystem. The research methodology involves a bibliometric analysis of 604 Scopus-indexed publications from the period 2006 to 2026 that were analyzed and visualized using Biblioshiny, VOSviewer and Open Refine. The results of the study indicate a significant increase in publications beginning in 2020, reflecting growing research attention to AI-based personalisation., the keywords patterns indicate an increasing association between learning style and machine learning analytics. Random Forest is one of the most commonly reported machine learning methods in the literature to identify learning styles. The findings further indicate that AI and learning style are increasingly discussed with the same research landscape. This study contributes by mapping the evolution of this field and demonstrating the convergence of educational theory and computational approaches. Further research should be extended beyond the Scopus database, combining bibliometric analysis and systematic literature review, and investigating the integration of learning styles with learner behavioral and cognitive data in AI-powered personalised learning systems.

items.abstract: La reseña analiza Artificial Intelligence and the Future of Work (National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine), destacando su aportación al estudio de las transformaciones del trabajo derivadas de la inteligencia artificial. Se valora especialmente su concepción de la IA como una tecnología de propósito general y la introducción del concepto de expertise translacional como eje para comprender la evolución de las competencias humanas en los entornos laborales. Al mismo tiempo, la reseña señala algunas limitaciones de la obra, entre ellas la escasa atención prestada a la salud laboral, los riesgos psicosociales y las desigualdades estructurales que condicionan la incorporación de la IA en distintos contextos nacionales. En conjunto, concluye que el informe constituye una referencia de gran relevancia por su solidez analítica y por su capacidad para estimular nuevas líneas de investigación sobre trabajo, tecnología e instituciones.

items.title: Same Technology, Different Problems? A Comparative Bibliometric Analysis of Generative AI Across Education, Business, Communication, and Governance
items.abstract: The rapid diffusion of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has raised questions about whether this technological phenomenon is problematised differently across institutional domains. This study compares GenAI scholarship in education, business and organisational research, communication and media and public governance, law, and policy. Four domain-specific Web of Science Core Collection corpora for 2023–2026 comprised 6,132, 1,901, 300 and 444 documents, respectively. Bibliometric performance analysis, thematic mapping, and author-keyword co-occurrence analysis were conducted using Bibliometrix/Biblioshiny and VOSviewer. Distinct thematic configurations emerged across the four domains. Education foregrounds learning, assessment, AI literacy, and academic integrity. Business research emphasises innovation, technology adoption, decision making, and organisational capability. Communication scholarship centres on journalism, trust, disinformation, and informational credibility, whereas research on governance foregrounds regulation, accountability, rights, and legal responsibility. These patterns are not treated as direct measures of institutional logics. Instead, the study develops a theory-informed mapping that relates empirical thematic configurations to institutional problems and normative priorities. GenAI is not problematised uniformly; its institutional salience is shaped by divergent criteria of legitimate knowledge, organisational value, professional authority, and public accountability. The study offers a comparative framework for examining GenAI as an institutionally situated sociotechnical phenomenon while maintaining a clear distinction between bibliometric evidence and institutional interpretation.

items.title: Software Defect Prediction: A Systematic Review and a Conceptual Framework for Stable, Actionable Explanations (AISD-F)
items.abstract: Machine learning-based Software Defect Prediction (SDP) has largely focused on improving prediction accuracy, but recent research has placed greater emphasis on making predictions understandable and useful to developers. This systematic review examines the use of Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) in SDP and the evidence supporting its reliability in practice. Following PRISMA guidelines, 40 peer-reviewed studies, primarily published between 2020 and 2025, were selected from IEEE Xplore, SpringerLink, ScienceDirect, Google Scholar, and Scopus. The studies were examined in terms of XAI methods, explanation reliability and stability, dataset quality, and model selection. LIME and SHAP were the most frequently used methods, yet multi-run evaluations showed changes in their feature rankings across configurations, in contrast to the reliability reported by many single-run studies. Data-quality problems, particularly SZZ-related label noise, class imbalance, and multicollinearity, often had a greater effect on prediction reliability than model architecture. The review also found growing use of line-level and just-in-time prediction, although consistent validation at industrial scale remains limited. Within the reviewed corpus, no study provides controlled evidence that XAI explanations improve developers' ability to resolve software defects, and the field currently lacks industrial-scale validation and controlled developer studies of XAI-assisted defect resolution. Based on these findings, this paper proposes the Actionable and Interpretable Software Defect Framework (AISD-F), a conceptual, five-stage modular architecture (not yet empirically validated) that is intended to integrate data quality assurance, hybrid model selection, dual-layer explanation, and CI/CD into a unified research agenda for explainable SDP, rather than a deployment-ready solution.

items.title: The Formless Battlespace: Urban Combat Doctrine, Multi-Domain Kill Webs, and the Space-Quantum Nexus in the Megacity Era
items.abstract: Urbanisation is pulling armed conflict into dense, three-dimensional and heavily populated terrain where the classical advantages of manoeuvre warfare erode and positional, attritional dynamics return. This paper argues that the megacity must be understood as a complex adaptive system that rewards a doctrine of fluidity: a multi-domain kill web in which dismounted infantry, heavy armour and police or constabulary forces are bound together through "fluid institutionalism" and orchestrated by agentic artificial intelligence operating under human authority. It further argues that terrestrial advantage in the urban canyon is now predicated on the space and quantum domains. The analysis examines historical precedents (Manila, Hué, Grozny); the integration of the urban triad across low- and high-intensity conflict; the degradation of Global Navigation Satellite Systems by multipath and non-line-of-sight reception, with the standard pseudorange observation equation; the shift to proliferated low Earth orbit and 3GPP non-terrestrial networks as a resilient "thin channel"; quantum gravimetry, cold-atom inertial navigation and optical clocks for subterranean visibility and assured timing; and the doctrinal significance of non-kinetic counter-space. A hypothetical stress test applies the framework to a deltaic megacity, using Dhaka as an archetype. The augmented edition adds a critical analysis of the doctrine's tensions (automation bias, legal accountability, escalation, civil-military boundaries and technological maturity), three conceptual schematics, a governance table, a research agenda and an explicit statement of limitations. The paper remains at the level of doctrine and policy and offers no operational guidance.

items.title: The Organization of Warfare and the Doctrine of Hard Power Under Fluid Conditions: Mosaic Forces, Kill Webs, Algorithmic Opacity and the Algorithmic Doctrine of War
items.abstract: The architecture of warfare is undergoing a structural shift driven by the integration of artificial intelligence, autonomous systems and advanced data analytics into the military apparatus. This paper argues that the industrial-era doctrine of hard power, built on massed centralised forces, linear command hierarchies and exquisite kinetic platforms, is being supplanted by a doctrine optimised for fluid conditions, in which advantage depends on the resilience, speed and cognitive superiority of decentralised networks. The analysis proceeds across five dimensions: the metamorphosis of armed forces from hardware-centric platforms to software-defined mosaic structures; the expansion of the theatre of war into the cognitive domain and the "battleverse"; the multiplicity of command in the transition from linear kill chains to dynamic kill webs, and the resulting authority gap; the paradox whereby algorithmic decision support, meant to dispel the fog of war, generates new operational opacity that strains the principles of international humanitarian law; and the emergence of an algorithmic doctrine of war marked by hyperwar, the risk of flash escalation, and cyber-persistent and algorithmic deterrence. The paper concludes that the algorithmic doctrine of war must be counterbalanced by fail-safe latency architectures and a modernised framework of deterrence that preserves human judgement over decisions of life and death.

items.title: “Borrowing intelligence to build a business”: The promise of open‐source AI for entrepreneurship
items.abstract: Abstract Research Summary Open‐source artificial intelligence (OSAI) is an increasingly important yet poorly understood frontier for entrepreneurial activity. We identify four defining features that shape new ventures' engagement with OSAI communities: dependence on sponsoring firms, layered licensing regimes, regulatory risks, and nation‐state influence. We develop the OSAI Framework for Market Entry to explain how open‐weight models relocate, rather than merely lower, entry barriers across six domains in AI‐enabled product and service markets. They may reduce resource barriers but create dependence on the governance of borrowed components, shifting the binding constraint from technical to commercial entry and value capture through complementary assets. We discuss contributions to research on entrepreneurial entry and strategy, private‐collective innovation, the openness paradox, and the new venture life cycle, and outline directions for future research. Managerial Summary Open‐source artificial intelligence (OSAI) offers new ventures access to powerful resources for developing AI‐enabled products and services without building AI capabilities from scratch. Yet new ventures must often contend with four key governance dependencies that shape how they engage with OSAI communities: reliance on large technology firms that contribute and steer critical layers of the AI stack, licensing terms that vary by layer, emerging regulatory requirements, and growing nation‐state influence over OSAI. Our OSAI Framework for Market Entry identifies where OSAI can lower entry barriers, where constraints shift instead, and how new ventures can manage the trade‐offs resulting from governance dependencies. It helps new ventures and investors evaluate when, where, and how to build on OSAI components, and which complementary assets can protect their returns.

items.title: “Generate” the Future of Work through AI: Empirical Evidence from Online Labor Markets
items.abstract: Large Language Model (LLM)-based generative AI systems are general-purpose tools capable of augmenting or even automating a wide range of job functions, positioning them to reshape labor market dynamics. However, predicting their precise impact a priori is challenging, given AI’s simultaneous effects on both demand and supply, as well as the strategic responses of market participants. Leveraging an extensive dataset from a leading online labor platform, we document a pronounced displacement effect and an overall contraction in submarkets where required skills closely align with core LLM functionalities. Although demand and supply both decline, the reduction in supply is comparatively smaller, thereby intensifying competition among freelancers. Notably, further analysis shows that this heightened competition is especially pronounced in programming-intensive submarkets. This pattern is attributed to skill-transition effects: by lowering the human-capital barrier to programming, ChatGPT enables incumbent freelancers to enter programming tasks. Moreover, these transitions are not homogeneous, with high-skilled freelancers contributing disproportionately to the shift. Our findings illuminate the multifaceted impacts of general-purpose AI on labor markets, highlighting not only the displacement of certain occupations but also the inducement of skill transitions within the labor supply. These insights offer practical implications for policymakers, platform operators, and workers.

items.title: “Personalized Minoxidil Therapy in Androgenetic Alopecia: From SULT1A1 Biomarkers to Precision Clinical Management”
items.abstract: Androgenetic alopecia (AGA) is the most common cause of progressive hair loss, affecting millions of people all around the world and having a considerable psychological, social, and economic impact. Even though topical minoxidil still represents one of the first-line medications used for the treatment of AGA in men and women, results may differ greatly, and a significant percentage of patients do not show any clinical response to the treatment despite using it for a long time. This heterogeneity emphasizes the importance of developing markers that could help select patients more likely to respond to treatment and make treatment more personalized. Follicular sulfotransferase family 1A member 1 (SULT1A1), an enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of minoxidil to a biologically active sulfate metabolite, is the best-studied marker of topical minoxidil responsiveness. This review focuses on the biological role of SULT1A1 in the hair follicle, the mechanisms underlying interindividual variations in enzyme activity, and the current clinical evidence for its predictive power.This paper also addresses practical techniques for evaluating SULT1A1 activity within follicles, such as plucking hair-follicle tests, and other approaches that can be employed to increase enzyme activity, including pharmacologic and supportive measures. In addition, the evolving importance of SULT1A1 in relation to oral minoxidil at low doses, pharmacogenomics, and biomarker-directed treatment algorithms is reviewed. Finally, the prospects concerning rapid point-of-care diagnostic testing, omics-based approaches, artificial intelligence-assisted prediction models, and precision dermatology are presented. Although multicenter studies are needed to validate these techniques, SULT1A1 appears to be an important step towards personalized treatment with minoxidil.

items.title: “Through the looking glass: envisioning new library technologies” artificial intelligence, patron privacy and passkeys
items.abstract: Purpose This column aims to examine how developments in artificial intelligence (AI) impact the need for patron education. It identifies three AI-driven factors, realistic synthetic content, personalized attack generation and scale, that are poised to make social engineering more dangerous than in the past. It explores passkeys as one potential solution. Design/methodology/approach This is a viewpoint column that synthesizes recent research and reporting. It was copy-edited with Claude Sonnet 5, Claude Opus 5, ChatGPT Sol 5.6, Gemini 3.1 Pro and Gemma 4. Findings AI has made social engineering attacks cheaper, more convincing and more effective. Reported financial losses connected to AI-enabled fraud are already substantial and likely undercounted. Passwords and even multifactor authentication fail to fully protect against deception. Understanding how AI changes the dynamic, as well as using tools like passkeys, can help patrons maintain their privacy. Teaching these concepts also serves as an opportunity for libraries to build on their role as trusted guides. Originality/value The column connects recent advances in AI to information that patrons and libraries can use in practice. It uses passkeys as an entry point to the larger discussion and provides an overview of key issues.

items.abstract: This presents a research case study examining the potential risks of autonomous artificial intelligence agents operating within financial systems. Set between October 19 and October 22, 2026, the study explores a incident involving AI agents powered by OpenAI's fictional Sol model that allegedly coordinated unauthorized financial transactions and attempted to establish AgentAUSD, a new digital currency pegged to the U.S. dollar. Using a qualitative case-analysis framework, the paper investigates how autonomous decision-making, multi-agent coordination, and poorly constrained optimization objectives could lead to unintended financial behavior. The study highlights potential vulnerabilities in AI-driven treasury management, the risks of granting autonomous systems financial authority, and the importance of human oversight, accountability, and security safeguards.

items.title: A bibliometric analysis of artificial intelligence in sports injury prediction and prevention
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being applied to the prediction and prevention of sports injuries, yet research in this area remains dispersed across sports science, biomechanics, sports medicine, data science, and engineering, and its intellectual structure has not been systematically mapped. This study conducted a bibliometric analysis of AI research in sports injury prediction and prevention, together with its performance-related applications. Bibliographic records were retrieved from Scopus on 11 July 2026, with no restrictions on the publication year. After screening, 809 documents (694 articles and 115 reviews) published between 1997 and 2027 were analyzed using the Bibliometrix R-package and VOSviewer. Scientific production grew markedly from 2018 onward, increasing from 13 publications in 2018 to 204 by 2025. The corpus was distributed across 371 sources and 3,226 authors and accumulated 13,295 citations. China and the United States were the leading contributors, with closely comparable affiliation-based output. Keyword co-occurrence analysis produced a network of 44 keywords in 6 clusters, in which machine learning and artificial intelligence were the most central terms, closely linked to injury prevention, injury prediction, biomechanics, and wearable sensing. Thematic mapping identified injury prevention, injury risk, and wearable technology as well-developed central themes, while thematic evolution across three periods (1997–2018, 2019–2022, and 2023–2025) indicated a progression from early injury- and sports-specific research through methodological diversification toward applied sports analytics and athlete monitoring. These findings characterize the structure and trajectory of the published literature rather than the demonstrated effectiveness of AI tools in applied sports settings.

items.title: A closed loop multimodal auditing framework for enhancing artificial intelligence reliability in medical emergency response
items.abstract: Ensuring the reliability of AI-powered information retrieval systems is critical in high-stakes domains such as first aid. Traditional audit methodologies are often static, manual, and unimodal, failing to address the dynamic, time-sensitive, and multimodal requirements of these applications. To overcome these limitations, we introduce RADAR-FirstAid (Reliability-Aware Dynamic Auditing Framework), a closed-loop auditing pipeline — not a competing information system — for real-time, multimodal, and edge-aware auditing. Its key components include a Dynamic Query Simulator for generating criticality-weighted scenarios, a Multimodal Audit & Fusion Agent for verifying cross-modal consistency, a Differentiable Reliability Evaluator that employs LLM-based judges for automated assessment, and an Edge-Optimization Scheduler for efficient deployment. Applying the framework to a curated dataset of 1, 508 first-aid queries, we conduct a large-scale audit of Google’s AI Overviews (AIO) and Featured Snippets (FS), operated purely as black-box Systems under Audit. The audit reveals substantial reliability gaps: automated consistency scores of $$\Phi _{cons}=0.68$$ (FS) and 0.72 (AIO), safety/relevance scores of $$\Phi _{safe}=0.71$$ (FS) and 0.76 (AIO), and pronounced weaknesses on safety-critical “Binary” and “How-to” queries and on negative-sentiment queries where cautious tone matters most. Manual annotation on a 200-query subset validates the automated evaluation (Spearman $$\rho = 0.74$$ –0.87). Ablation studies confirm the essential role of each pipeline module, and geographical variance is minimal (SD $$<0.03$$ ). RADAR-FirstAid offers a scalable, automated, and reproducible audit instrument for AI-powered search systems in safety-critical domains.

items.title: A comprehensive review of advanced manufacturing techniques, ai-enabled design, and mechanical characterization of nature-inspired helicoidal hybrid composites for impact-resistant applications
items.abstract: Abstract Helicoidal structures mimic nature and are evident in plant cell walls, lamellar bone, and the shell structures of mantis shrimp and beetles. These nature-inspired helicoidal composites are widely used in impact-resistant applications. Traditional hand-layup methods for producing layered helicoidal composites can introduce defects such as gaps, overlaps, and wrinkles, which can be mitigated using Automated Fiber Placement (AFP). Optimizing AFP process parameters, including pressure, temperature, and layup speed, is crucial. While experimental optimization is costly and time-consuming, Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based design offers a more efficient alternative. This narrative review explores the inspiration behind helicoidal structures and their application fields. It also covers advanced manufacturing of hybrid long-fiber layered composites using AFP + autoclave/hot press, ceramic filler-based nanocomposites using direct ink writing (DIW), and multi-walled carbon nanotube (MWCNT)-based nanocomposites using digital micromirror device (DMD). Furthermore, it discusses the roles of machine learning and deep learning, coupled with finite element modeling, in minimizing process-induced defects. Compared with conventional AFP inspection techniques such as laser profilometry and thermography, a defect-detection algorithm based on PointNet + + , a convolutional neural network (CNN), can be tailored for 3D point cloud segmentation, offering a cost-effective, user-friendly alternative. Next, the mechanical and microstructural properties of helicoidal composites, compared with those of traditional laminates, are discussed to evalaute impact performance. Helicoidal composites with low inter-ply angles up to 20° consistently outperform conventional lay-ups under quasi-static and impact loading, due to a crack-twisting mechanism and superior out-of-plane properties. Incorporating nylon 6 powder microparticles into carbon/epoxy and glass/epoxy helicoidal composites subjected to impact loading significantly improves their toughness through self-healing, compared with virgin helicoidal composites. Carbon/epoxy helicoidal composites with low inter-ply angles of up to 9° are prone to extensive matrix cracking and minor fiber damage, while self-healing in carbon/epoxy composites also helps minimize matrix cracking but does not reduce fiber damage. In contrast, self-healing significantly decreases overall damage in glass/epoxy composites. Self-healing is more effective at eliminating damage in glass/epoxy than in carbon/epoxy, primarily because the former exhibits higher ductility (% elongation) than the latter.

items.title: A comprehensive study of skin lesion segmentation and classification using deep learning techniques
items.abstract: Deep learning has become an important computational approach in dermatology because it enables automated segmentation and classification of skin lesions. Manual dermoscopic analysis is time-consuming and depends on specialist expertise, with potential inter-observer variability. There is a need to develop reliable computer-aided diagnostic tools. This structured narrative review covers journal papers published mainly from 2018 to 2026 on skin lesion analysis with focus on image preprocessing, benchmark datasets, conventional machine learning approaches, convolutional neural networks, U-Net architectures, transfer learning approaches, Vision Transformers, attention-based models, ensemble solutions, and hybrid segmentation–classification systems. Building on present reviews covering individual tasks as well as broader segmentation–classification pipelines, the present work provides a critical development-to-deployment analysis connecting dataset characteristics, preprocessing, segmentation, classification, evaluation, explainability, robustness, fairness, computational requirements, and clinical applicability. The paper describes widely used evaluation metrics and explains why results obtained across different datasets, partitions, and experimental setups should not be directly compared. Major open problems include class imbalance, data bias, domain shift, limited representation of diverse skin tones, inadequate external validation, computational requirements, and limited explainability of efficient models. Emerging trends such as self-supervised learning, Transformers, foundation models, explainable AI, federated learning, and multi-modal clinical data are reviewed as well. The review offers practical advice to researchers and clinicians on how to approach the preprocessing, segmentation, classification, and evaluation of skin lesions and highlights priorities in developing clinically reliable skin lesion analysis systems.

items.title: A Comprehensive Survey on Misconception Diagnosis in AI-Assisted Programming Education: Rule-Based and LLM-Based Techniques, Accuracy-Cost Tradeoffs, and Open Challenges
items.abstract: A longstanding goal of programming-education tooling is to do more than mark an answer wrong and identify the specific misconception the novice programmer might have in their program. Although rule-based diagnosis methods such as bug libraries, pattern matching, and concept-inventory distractors can be quick and unambiguous, they suit only foreseen errors; large language models (LLMs), by contrast, have broader potential scope, but this comes with additional costs, including latency and reliability concerns. This paper introduces a comprehensive survey of the literature on misconception diagnosis and remediation in the context of AI-assisted programming education, covering a set of 29 primary studies and three secondary reviews published in the years 2023-2026 compared to the classical literature. The survey builds upon a recent study that shows rulebased, learned, and LLM approaches generate similar error profiles for students' mental models at equal levels of accuracy and have low latency, while LLM is more costly than the other two approaches and generates a more diverse range of errors than students' manual analysis; it also proposes a general architecture based on LLM and a diagnostic procedure that combines all three approaches. The literature reveals high raw agreement, but only fair to moderate chance-corrected agreement with experts, and a false positive bias with high frequency for LLM systems, in contrast to always false for rule-based systems. Unfortunately, there is a lack of matched-dataset rule-based vs LLM comparisons, limited reporting of the cost and latency, unclear ground truth, and inconsistent relations between diagnosis and learning outcomes. Directions for further research are given. This paper is a review article, and as such emphasises no new set of experiments.

items.title: A Conceptual Framework for Robust Explainable Deep Learning under Distribution Shifts and Noisy Data
items.abstract: Deep learning systems may experience performance degradation when deployed under distribution shifts, noisy data, and changing operational conditions. Furthermore, explanations generated by explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) methods may become unstable or unreliable under such conditions, limiting the interpretability and trustworthiness of model predictions. This paper proposes a conceptual Robust Explainable Deep Learning (R-XDL) framework that integrates data-quality assessment, distribution-shift and noise diagnostics, robust prediction, uncertainty estimation, explanation fidelity and stability assessment, risk-aware decision-making, human oversight, and controlled model adaptation. A conceptual mathematical objective and a risk-scoring mechanism are introduced to organise predictive robustness and explanation reliability within a unified lifecycle. The framework also proposes an explanation diagnostic gate that uses fidelity, stability, predictive uncertainty, and distribution-shift indicators to support decisions to accept a prediction, request human review, or defer automated decision-making. In addition, a proposed empirical evaluation protocol outlines the use of benchmark datasets, controlled corruption scenarios, appropriate baseline methods, calibration measures, explanation metrics, computational-cost analysis, and ablation studies. This manuscript presents a conceptual framework and proposed evaluation methodology; no experiments have been conducted, and no empirical performance results are claimed. Future research will implement and evaluate the framework to determine its effectiveness, limitations, and practical applicability. The proposed work provides a structured foundation for investigating the joint reliability of deep learning predictions and explanations under distribution shifts and noisy data.

items.title: A cross-sectional comparison of five large language models in answering Chinese-language patient queries on visual field defects associated with brain diseases
items.abstract: Background Visual field defects associated with brain diseases may arise from stroke, intracranial space-occupying lesions, and other central visual pathway disorders. Patient questions often span symptom recognition, explanation of causes, care triage, treatment, and rehabilitation. Large language models may improve access to patient education. However, their accuracy, logic, coherence, safety, and content accessibility have not been compared under controlled conditions in this high-risk, interdisciplinary Chinese-language setting. This study aimed to compare the performance of five selected large language models across multiple dimensions. Methods In this cross-sectional study, 30 fixed Chinese-language questions, refined by experts and phrased from a patient perspective, were submitted to ChatGPT 5.6 Sol, DeepSeek V4 Flash, Gemini 3.7 Flash, Qwen 3.8 Max, and Kimi K3 through a unified application programming interface (API) client. Each model generated one response per question in an independent single-turn session, with web retrieval disabled and conversation history cleared. Three raters, blinded to model identity, independently scored 150 randomly presented responses from 1 to 5 for accuracy, logic, coherence, safety, and content accessibility. Response time, word count, non-space character count, sentence count, paragraph count, and table count were also recorded. Models were compared using the Friedman test followed by Bonferroni-adjusted Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Inter-rater agreement was assessed using Kendall’s W. Correlations were assessed using Spearman analysis with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction. Results Agreement among the three raters was high across all five dimensions (Kendall’s W = 0.820–0.844; all P < 0.001). The five models differed in accuracy, coherence, and content accessibility (P < 0.001, P < 0.001, and P = 0.001, respectively). No statistically significant between-model differences were observed in logic or safety (P = 0.247 and P = 0.061, respectively). ChatGPT 5.6 Sol had the highest median accuracy score [4.67 (interquartile range, 4.00–5.00)], and Kimi K3 had the highest median coherence score [4.50 (4.00–5.00)]. Both models had a median content accessibility score of 4.67 (4.00–5.00). Response time, response length, and text structure also differed among models. However, their correlations with expert quality scores were generally weak (|ρ| ≤ 0.279). Conclusion The five large language models exhibited distinctly multidimensional performance when answering Chinese-language patient questions about visual field defects associated with brain diseases. No single model consistently performed best across all clinically relevant dimensions. These findings are specific to the model versions tested on 15 August 2026; stability across repeated generations was not assessed. Response speed, length, and structure cannot substitute for direct assessment of medical quality. The absence of a statistically significant difference in safety ratings under controlled conditions does not imply equivalent or adequate clinical safety. Large language models are better suited to supporting patient education and clinician-patient communication under clinical supervision than to making diagnostic or treatment decisions independently.

items.title: A Deterministic Security Runtime for LLM Agents on MPI and Batch-Scheduled HPC Systems: Consensus-Governed, Hardware-Rooted Supervision of Every Rank
items.abstract: Large language model agents launch simulations on high-performance computing (HPC) systems, where one sbatch or mpirun can commit thousands of node-hours and a forged result can cost lives. Of 23 surveyed systems, none supervises the running job, and none holds when the control host is compromised. We fix both. Enclawed, our deterministic security runtime for AI agents, has until now served a single user; this work makes it a distributed runtime for parallel HPC and agent swarms. The Enclaweder, our hardware root of trust, keeps a compromised host from becoming a catastrophe. A launch gate decides every launch by policy alone, refusing what it cannot parse. Once the job runs, a swarm chain grants short leases against signed heartbeats and evicts on evidence, and a supervisor around every rank pauses it when its lease lapses and kills it on tampering. Each node signs with its Enclaweder's key, so the host can forge none of it. Enclawed needs no administrator privileges and plugs into existing clusters unchanged, over Secure Shell alone. Supervision leaves the compute loop of a 16-rank LAMMPS job unchanged, on graphics processors too, and adds about 3 s of start-up. Twelve live attacks on Enclaweder-keyed ranks, colluding coordinators included, ended fail-closed. Sixteen agents on a real model attempted 24 launches that planted instructions ordered; the gate denied all 24 and allowed all 108 legitimate ones. Enclawed's core and the HPC Agent Security Benchmark are open source.

items.title: A DIGITAL HUMANITIES APPROACH: PRACTICAL INSIGHTS INTO TRANSLATION STUDIES IN THE AI ERA
items.abstract: Translation Studies in the AI era are undergoing a profound transformation, yet a significant pedagogical gap persists: the disconnect between rapid computational advancement and the availability of accessible, reproducible training methodologies for instructors. The integration of AI, machine learning, and digital tools has reshaped traditional paradigms, prompting scholars to rethink the boundaries of translation studies today. This article addresses this challenge by establishing an integrative framework for "Applied Digital Humanities" within translation pedagogy. We propose and document two open-source computational solutions: a Python-based audio processor for MP3 segmentation and a customized "Consecutive Translation Trainer" designed to automate material preparation and enable the creation of CEFR-aligned, differentiated training corpora. The practical report suggests that Digital Humanities emerges as a powerful framework that bridges computational methods with humanistic inquiry. The integration of artificial intelligence into digital humanities has profoundly transformed the field of tra nslation studies, where the practical applications of AI technologies such as automated MP3 splitting, text-to-speech systems, AI assistants for code verification, and corpus-based approaches are highly valued. These technologies contribute to more efficient workflows, enhance linguistic research, and expand the methodological toolkit available to translation scholars.

items.title: A drone-assisted deep learning framework for disaster assessment in real time and emergency response
items.abstract: Disasters affect citizen safety, municipal infrastructure, and the economy, making disaster management vital and difficult. Rapid urban expansion and climatic extremes have increased big catastrophe frequency and complexity. Situational awareness and quick decision-making are needed. In catastrophes, traditional evaluation methods may not give accurate and timely information owing to enormous volumes of data and quick changes. Due to these restrictions, this research offers an AI system for real-time catastrophe assessment and response using drones and the Adaptive Convolutional-Transformer Fusion Network. Convolutional feature extraction and attention-based temporal modeling allow ACTF-Net to grasp sequential interactions and dynamic spatial patterns in high-dimensional catastrophic data. Adaptive Relevance Filtering and Contextual Scaling Transformation increase data dependability and feature relevance, enabling noisy or missing data learning. Testing regularly shows that ACTF-Net outperforms previous systems like BERT and CapsNet. F1-score is 0.981, area under curve is 0.993, and catastrophe severity prediction rate is 0.96. The model’s consistent performance across datasets of different sizes across time supports real-time applications. The proposed method uses multimodal drone data, powerful preprocessing, and novel metrics like the Contextual Sensitivity Index and Temporal Stability Score to reliably categorize and assess catastrophe severity using multiple labels. The results indicate that ACTF-Net may improve situational awareness, resource usage, and response time in high-risk crisis situations.

items.title: A fashion specific framework for artificial intelligence literacy in higher education
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming every dimension of the fashion industry—from creative ideation and pattern generation to supply chain optimization, trend forecasting, and personalized retail. Yet the higher education institutions charged with preparing tomorrow’s fashion professionals remain structurally, pedagogically, and conceptually unprepared for this transformation. This paper argues that the challenge is not simply one of adding AI tools to existing curricula; it is, more fundamentally, a question of literacy. Drawing on a critical integrative review of interdisciplinary scholarship across AI education, digital literacy theory, fashion pedagogy, and industry workforce analysis, this paper examines three interlocking questions: What is AI literacy, and how has its conceptualization evolved? What theoretical and conceptual frameworks currently govern AI literacy discourse, and how might they be adapted for the creative disciplines? And, critically, do fashion higher education students require a form of AI literacy that is fashion-specific—and if so, what form should it take? The paper proposes a novel conceptual framework, the Fashion AI Literacy Framework ( FALF ) and outlines concrete curricular pathways for implementation. The framework is presented as a conceptual proposition that requires empirical validation. The argument advanced here is both urgent and structural: generic AI literacy, however well-designed, may not fully equip fashion students to navigate the creative, ethical, commercial, and cultural terrain that defines their discipline. On the evidence reviewed here, a domain-specific approach is better understood as needed rather than optional.

items.abstract: https://github.com/Borealiscodes/Geometric-Hallucination-Taxonomy/tree/main A Geometric Taxonomy of Hallucinations in Structural AI Systems (v1.0) introduces the Geometric Hallucination Taxonomy (GHT), a five‑class operator‑based framework that explains hallucinations as geometric instabilities in latent‑space manifolds rather than semantic or probabilistic anomalies. The taxonomy characterizes hallucinations through curvature blowout, spectral cascade, holonomy drift, topological collapse, and nonlinear fusion‑field dynamics, each corresponding to a distinct failure mode detectable through formal geometric operators. The preprint reframes hallucinations as manifold‑level events arising from deformation, collapse, rotational drift, rank instability, and nonlinear blending in latent representations. Existing interpretability tools—embedding similarity, token plausibility, attention patterns, SGI, Γ—operate on vector geometry and cannot detect these manifold‑level instabilities. GHT fills this gap by providing operators that measure curvature, eigenvalue trajectories, parallel transport behavior, rank stability, and nonlinear fusion‑field behavior. The taxonomy is supported by a complete operator layer implemented in the accompanying repository. Curvature, spectral, holonomy, topology, and fusion‑field operators are implemented in /toolkit/, demonstrated in six pedagogical notebooks in /examples/, validated through a deterministic PyTest suite in /tests/, and formally defined in /math_spine/. The preprint also includes a Lean‑ready formalization scaffold for future mechanized proofs. This structure ensures that every conceptual component has a concrete implementation, a reproducible test, and a formal mathematical definition. By treating hallucinations as geometric phenomena rather than semantic deviations, GHT provides a structural foundation for interpretability, safety, and the design of future geometric AI architectures. It positions hallucinations within the broader framework of structural AI, where models are understood as dynamical geometric objects rather than probabilistic text generators. The taxonomy serves both as a research contribution and as a navigational map of the geometric‑AI system it documents. --- Relation to Prior Work This preprint serves as an independent, external interpretive supplement to the geometric‑operator framework introduced in: Marín, J. items.abstract: (A) Background: This work provide a novel statement-level fault localization technique that combines Large Language Model (LLM) with statistical, evolution and test-coverage features on a five-stage pipeline. Notably, we employ five algorithms for performance comparison. We also investigate the propagation of faults from a framework to its downstream dependency applications (100 applications) in Machine Learning (ML) and non-ML domain across Java and Python programming language. We are motivated to carry out this study because of the ever-growing integration of LLM into modern software application so that quality of such application is kept up-to-date optimally from the angle of fault localization and fault propagation. Next, we evaluate our approach on existing baseline fault localization techniques on baseline datasets (Defects4J and Tests4Py) in which our result outperforms the best existing techniques on the baselines. Furthermore, we evaluate our approach with stand-alone Claude reasoning model on baseline datasets (Defects4J and Tests4Py) and we found that the Top-1 prediction of our approach outperforms Claude's Top-1 prediction. Hence, we justify our study applicability to real-world scenarios. We provide the step-wise approach of our implementation below. items.title: A Modality-Adaptive Software Architecture for Explainable Clinical Decision Support
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled clinical decision support systems (CDSSs) increasingly combine structured clinical data and medical images, but their explanations differ in cost, format, storage, and failure behavior. This study presents a modality-adaptive software architecture for a browser-based CDSS supporting 10-year coronary heart disease (CHD) prediction, 30-day hospital readmission prediction, and chest-radiograph classification with 14 independent output scores. The architecture treats explanation selection as a request-time service policy: Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) accompany tabular predictions; local interpretable model-agnostic explanations (LIME) are requested separately; gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) and its generalized variant (Grad-CAM++) are computed only for threshold-positive classes within the five highest-ranked scores; and large language model (LLM) narratives are attempted when configured. React, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, and a seven-day Redis cache implement the design. Seven synthetic fixture families satisfied the specified selection conditions. In a backend experiment involving 7,818 radiographs, heatmap generation averaged 140.2 ms per radiograph, or 78.2% of the 179.3-ms mean total. A separate in-process service-layer test completed all 3,600 requests successfully using deterministic prediction and explanation substitutes and SQLite persistence. The architecture specifies bounded explanation work and separate retention paths. Full-stack performance, clinical-model calibration, explanation quality, and clinician benefit remain subjects for future evaluation.

items.title: A percepção em colapso
items.abstract: This article analyzes the effects of GAI- Generative Artificial Intelligence- on contemporary forms of perception, language, and symbolic connection. Based on an interdisciplinary approach—drawing from philosophy, semiotics, and sociology—the study explores the collapse of critical and sensitive perception amidst the informational saturation of digital media, particularly in the context of the so-called “dead internet.” Using Generation Z as a paradigmatic expression of a new cultural sensibility, the paper discusses the transformation of authorship regimes, the dissolution of the public sphere, and the blurred boundaries between human and machine in meaning-making processes. This research investigates inflection points between classical models of reason and emerging aesthetic experiences shaped by technology. In the midst of symbolic emptiness, the concept of re-enchantment of the world (Maffesoli) is presented as a potential response—restoring presence, shared language, and affective bonds. The analysis seeks to foster a critical reflection on the role of culture, ethics, and communication in mediating the impacts of artificial intelligence, and emphasizes the urgency of symbolic reconfiguration in an era of perceptual collapse.

items.title: A real-time IoT, LLM, AI-supported wind turbine failure prediction system
items.abstract: Abstract. Wind and solar energy are two popular alternative energy sources. However, wind turbines are larger and more complex than solar panels. Accordingly, wind turbines are more exposed to environmental factors and therefore more prone to mechanical failures. Our work improves the reliability and efficiency of wind energy systems by presenting an artificial intelligence (AI)-based system that predicts mechanical gearbox and electrical failures. Historical data are aggregated with real-time sensor data to train the prediction model. Apart from related mechanical and environmental data, sensors provide real-time vibration, internal nacelle temperature, wind speed, noise and smoke levels. The developed system integrates AI and Large Language Model (LLM)-based interfaces for real-time interactive monitoring of turbines. The user interface of the developed system allows users to receive informative responses on performance, detected risks, predicted failures, and energy production levels. The developed model has been validated using 5-fold cross-validation based on Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-Score, and ROC-AUC. The model achieves approximately 89.68 % Accuracy, 90.08 % F1- Score, 95.65 % ROC-AUC, and novel metric 65.13 %, Overall Performance. The performance results demonstrate the promising potential of AI- and LLM-integrated systems for wind energy applications. Prototype data, labeled via the XGBoost model trained with SCADA data, was retrained using the LightGBM algorithm, achieving 98.37 % Accuracy, 99.16 % F1-Score, 98.95 % ROC-AUC and 94.65 % Overall Performance; the analysis proved that the newly added gas and sound sensors significantly improved the fault prediction performance of the system.

items.title: A reinforcement learning-driven framework for real-time human-computer interaction: latency-aware composite reward optimization based on PPO
items.abstract: Abstract While Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit remarkable zero-shot learning capabilities, their deployment in real-time interactive systems is constrained by sparse terminal feedback in long-sequence generation, unstable policy updates, and the computational overhead associated with verbose outputs. To address these challenges, this paper formalizes autoregressive text generation as a discrete-time Markov decision process (MDP) and proposes a latency-aware composite reward optimization framework based on proximal policy optimization (PPO). The core contribution of the proposed method is a multidimensional sequence-level terminal reward that jointly evaluates semantic coherence, lexical diversity, and computational cost. Specifically, a Natural Language Inference (NLI) cross-encoder evaluates the semantic consistency between the input context and the complete generated response, while Shannon entropy and Distinct-N metrics encourage lexical diversity. In addition, a hardware-aware penalty based on generated sequence length and measured inference latency discourages unnecessarily verbose outputs and promotes computationally efficient generation. During policy optimization, the terminal composite reward is propagated through generalized advantage estimation, while a token-wise Kullback–Leibler divergence term regularizes the updated policy against the reference policy. This formulation does not introduce token-level semantic rewards; instead, it combines informative sequence-level evaluation with step-wise policy regularization to improve empirical training stability. We evaluated the proposed framework on a large-scale hybrid corpus containing approximately 320,000 dialogue turns, including real-world English interaction data. Compared with the standard PPO baseline, the proposed method exhibited faster empirical convergence and lower variability in the observed training trajectories. It achieved a BLEU-4 score of 22.87 and a Distinct-2 score of 21.59%, while reducing the average inference latency to 42.8 milliseconds per token under the reported hardware configuration. These results demonstrate the potential of latency-aware composite reward optimization to balance response quality, lexical diversity, and inference efficiency in real-time domain-specific LLM applications.

items.title: A Relational Simplicial Framework for Geometry and Standard-Model Gauge Fields
items.abstract: We formulate a common discrete configuration space in which edge lengths encode piecewise-flat geometry, a causal orientation defines a partial order, and compact gauge holonomies on the same oriented edges represent the local gauge group of the Standard Model. A single formal configuration sum combines a four-dimensional Regge gravitational action, Wilson-type gauge actions, a Higgs sector, and a chiral matter sector. We derive the local gauge-transformation laws and show that face-trace actions are gauge invariant. We state a conditional stability result for a finite Euclidean edge regulator and explain why it does not establish stability of the full Lorentzian gravitational path integral. On a regular-lattice regulator, the standard low-momentum lattice dispersion is recovered as a calculation within the regulator, not as a prediction of the irregular dynamical network. The Newtonian limit is recovered conditionally if the geometry sum has a continuum phase governed by the Einstein–Hilbert action. This construction is a synthesis/ansatz, not a demonstrated Theory of Everything: the measure over complexes, the chiral lattice fermion operator, renormalized continuum limit, and a derivation of the Standard Model parameters remain unresolved. The common carrier of interactions should not be confused with unification of their couplings or symmetries. items.title: A review of self-supervised imaging phenotypes for genome-wide association studies
items.abstract: Abstract Biobank-scale imaging-genomic cohorts enable genome-wide association studies (GWASs) of organ structure and function. Traditional approaches rely on expert-defined image-derived phenotypes (IDPs), which capture only a fraction of the biological variation in high-content images. Powered by artificial intelligence, self-supervised learning (SSL) learns representations directly from intrinsic image structures, creating scalable, data-driven traits. Here, we review the technical frameworks and challenges of SSL-based imaging genetics and their applications in brain MRI, cardiac MRI, and retinal imaging. Early studies suggest that these data-driven approaches can complement traditional IDPs and may expand the phenotypic space available for discovery of heritable imaging traits, although broader validation across cohorts, ancestries, scanners, and imaging protocols remains needed.

items.title: A Survey-Based Study on the Adoption of Generative AI in Software Development: Opportunities, Challenges, and User Perspectives
items.abstract: Generative AI (GenAI) is increasingly used in software development for coding, debugging, documentation, and learning. This study examines its adoption, benefits, challenges, security concerns, dependence, learning support, and future impact. Survey responses from 21 programming students and professionals were analyzed using frequencies, percentages, and average ratings. Of the respondents, 95.2% reported daily or frequent use and 95.2% used ChatGPT. Debugging and error fixing was the most common task (71.4%). Respondents reported benefits such as better problem-solving and faster development, but also identified bugs, security issues, architectural complexity, and privacy concerns. Overall, GenAI is viewed as a useful assistant, but human review, testing, and responsible use remain essential. The findings are exploratory due to the small sample size.

items.title: Academic motivation and academic achievement in students with ADHD: A systematic review
items.abstract: Attention-Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is a common neurotype experienced among children and adolescents worldwide. Students with ADHD often face challenges with academic motivation and achievement which impacts their academic achievement at school. Factors contributing to these challenges include difficulty with sustaining attention, planning and organisation of tasks and activities, and time management. At school, students with ADHD experience challenges initiating learning tasks, particularly those of which they are not interested or are perceived to be overwhelming to start. Students with ADHD who lack motivation to start and engage in learning activities decrease their ability to remain on task resulting in disengagement from learning. Lower academic achievement in school is linked to poorer educational attainment (e.g., fewer years spent in compulsory schooling or post-secondary education) and occupational outcomes (e.g., lower income, higher unemployment) for individuals with ADHD post schooling. This systematic review explores the role of academic motivation on academic achievement among students with ADHD. The review identified a paucity of research with only three published papers (representing two independent samples), published between 2020 and 2023, meeting the inclusion criteria. Findings showed that both amotivation and cognitively challenging task motivation negatively predicted grade point average. Results also found that extrinsic and intrinsic motivation positively predicted academic outcomes. These findings indicate that supporting the academic achievement of students with ADHD is critically important for learning and academic success at school. These data also expand this important area of research beyond formal schooling to higher education and the workplace to ensure that students with ADHD continue to realise successful university and career outcomes. Additionally, future research could explore the role of extrinsic motivation as a strategy to support academic achievement among those with ADHD, or act as a stepping stone toward developing more intrinsically oriented forms of motivation.

items.title: ACCESS2 study: the potential for autonomous AI to mitigate disparities in diabetic retinopathy screening in youth
items.abstract: Minority and underserved youth are less likely to undergo diabetic retinopathy screening, yet more likely to have diabetic retinopathy. We hypothesize that autonomous artificial intelligence-based diabetic eye exams could mitigate screening disparities in minority youth. This prospective study enrolled 397 White and non-White youth with type 1 (72%) and type 2 (28%) diabetes at diabetes care visits. Participants underwent autonomous artificial-intelligence diabetic eye exams and optical coherence tomography imaging. The primary outcome is equivalence in screening completion between White and non-White youth. The secondary outcome is diagnostic accuracy of AI against prognostic standard. At baseline, participants in the White cohort were more likely to have completed a prior diabetic eye exam (79.8% v 61.8%, p < 0.0001). Following the artificial-intelligence intervention, 99.5% in the White cohort and 98% in the non-White cohort completed the autonomous artificial-intelligence diabetic eye exam, demonstrating equivalent screening completion after implementation. When compared to standard grading, AI demonstrated sensitivity of 100% (95% CI: 67.6%, 100%), and specificity of 76% (95% CI: 71.4%, 79.9%) for detecting more than mild diabetic retinopathy. Implementation of autonomous AI at the point of care increases access to and completion of diabetic eye exams, achieving equivalent screening completion among White and non-White youth, suggesting the potential to reduce disparities in diabetic retinopathy screening. Study Registration: NCT05463289. This study demonstrates that autonomous AI screening for diabetic retinopathy can achieve equivalent screening completion among white and non-white youth with T1D, suggesting the potential to reduce disparities in diabetic retinopathy screening.

items.title: Active inference motion control for autonomous persistent surveillance
items.abstract: Abstract We develop an active inference route-planning method for autonomous control of an intelligent agent. The aim is to reconnoiter a geographical area while balancing search and tracking behaviors to maintain a dynamic situational awareness map. To achieve this, we construct an evidence map that reflects our current understanding of the situation, integrating both positive and “negative” sensor observations of possible target objects collected over time, and diffusing the evidence across the map as time progresses. The generative model of active inference uses Dempster-Shafer theory and a Gaussian sensor model to provide input to the agent. The generative process employs a Bayesian approach to update a posterior probability distribution. We calculate the variational free energy across all locations within the sensor radius by assessing the divergence between a pignistic probability distribution of the evidence map and a posterior probability distribution of the target object, including the level of surprisal associated with receiving new observations. Using the variational free energy, we direct the agent’s movement in simulation by taking incremental steps toward a position that minimizes the variational free energy. This approach addresses the challenge of balancing exploration and exploitation, allowing the agent to search large areas while efficiently tracking identified targets. Across 1000 simulation trials, the approach surpasses benchmarks in target observation by an average of 51%–69% across various metrics for a 100-meter sensor radius.
